    AI Overview
    The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is a Cabinet-level federal agency providing comprehensive healthcare, disability compensation, education assistance, home loans, and burial benefits to eligible military veterans and their families. Established in 1988, it operates medical centers, clinics, and national cemeteries nationwide. Contact the VA at 800-698-2411 or visit VA.gov for assistance. 
    Key Components and Services
    The VA is structured into three primary administrations: 
    • Veterans Health Administration (VHA): Operates 170 medical centers and numerous outpatient clinics, providing healthcare, nursing homes, and specialized medical services
      .
    • Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA): Manages non-healthcare benefits, including disability compensation, pension, education/training (GI Bill), and vocational rehabilitation.
    • National Cemetery Administration (NCA): Provides burial and memorial benefits to eligible veterans and family members at 135 national cemeteries. 
    Eligibility and Access 
    • Veteran Status: Generally requires active military service and a discharge that is not dishonorable.
    • Services: Offers support such as home loan guarantees, life insurance, and specialized services for disabled veterans.
    • Support: For immediate assistance with benefits or health services, veterans can use the VA.gov facility locator or call the main hotline at 800-698-2411. 
    Other Resources 
    • Ask VA (AVA): An online tool to find answers and submit questions.
    • National Personnel Records Center: For requesting military service records or replacing medals.
    • VA News: Provides updates on technology and services.
